decision: Use TypeScript for a dependency-free presentation function consuming the existing aggregate SDK view. Localize fixed text for en and sv-SE, and reject malformed projections to UNKNOWN. No frontend framework or bundler is selected by this component.
constraints: Deterministic synchronous presentation of a bounded aggregate; no raw frames, tracks, identifiers, persistence or transport.
Node-verifiable ESM, portable browser output with no Node imports; future UI must call with a fresh SDK view.
Runtime validation remains in application code; static types alone cannot authorize data.
Avoid dependencies at runtime and preserve versioned API-v1 vocabulary.

alternatives.assessment: Selected: explicit status/locale unions plus ordinary ECMAScript runtime guards; direct integration with the SDK declaration boundary. No numeric kernel or new runtime needed.
Same runtime possible but loses this boundary's static locale and status contract unless a separate declaration or annotation check is added.

Credible closed-state model, but JS ports/interop would still be required for the existing host SDK; this small synchronous presenter gains no demonstrated runtime guard or capability from that boundary.
Useful candidate for future DOM integration. Rendering and custom-element lifecycle are outside this presentation function; adding its runtime now would not enforce input semantics.
Can compile a strongly typed presenter to JS. The existing SDK still needs external/runtime admission. No material runtime or interoperability improvement established for these three display states.

limits: Not a UI application, Help Center, role system, source authenticator or P19 acceptance.
A stale previously returned view has no new freshness guarantee; renderer must request a fresh SDK view.
Direct object snapshot happens before shape validation; no pre-clone byte or process-memory bound.
Finite two-coordinate covariance is checked for shape only and then discarded; no accuracy or physical calibration claim.
No hard real-time, MLS/CNSA, DDS/Link16, uptime or tactical deployment qualification.
